basic_information.short_title: Continuing Validity of the 2020–2023 Special Development Fund
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT FURTHER CONTINUING THE VALIDITY OF THE 2020, 2021, 2022, AND 2023 SPECIAL DEVELOPMENT FUND, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: Immediately after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Extends 4 years of Special Development Fund money — 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023 — and removes the deadline for actually spending it: the funds stay disbursable “until fully expended”.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: Development projects funded from four successive Special Development Funds were still unfinished, and the earlier extensions were themselves running out.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Release and obligation deadlines move to 31 December 2024 for the 2020–2022 funds and 31 December 2025 for the 2023 fund. In every case, disbursement continues until the money is fully expended, with no end date.
who_will_be_affected: Communities with projects funded from any Special Development Fund since 2020
Bangsamoro ministries and offices administering the funds
Taxpayers, given the scale of the money and the removal of a spending deadline
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: Took effect immediately on publication at the end of 2023.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. 4 years of development money can be committed until end-2024 (2025 for the 2023 fund) — and once committed, there is no deadline to spend it. It stays available until fully expended.
in_practice: 2020 and 2021 Special Development Fund: available for release and obligation until 31 December 2024
2022 Special Development Fund: available for release and obligation until 31 December 2024
2023 Special Development Fund: available for release and obligation until 31 December 2025
In all three cases the money continues to be available for disbursement until fully expended
All other provisions of the underlying appropriations acts remain in force
The Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management issues implementing guidelines

for_specific_groups.Communities awaiting projects: Work funded from any of these 4 years did not have to be abandoned.
for_specific_groups.Contractors: No payment deadline applies once the appropriation is obligated.
for_specific_groups.Anyone tracking public money: This is the provision that matters — the disbursement deadline is gone, so these funds no longer lapse by effluxion of time.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The Bangsamoro Special Development Fund for 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: In force since the end of 2023.
what_you_can_do: Ask which Special Development Fund year a local project draws on, and whether the money has been obligated
Read alongside BAA 22, 23 and 32, which appropriated the funds, and BAA 34, the earlier extension
watch_out_for: “Until fully expended” removes any outer limit on when the money must actually be paid out — the ordinary discipline of a cash budgeting system does not apply to these funds.
The act states no amounts; the sums sit in the underlying appropriations acts.
No reporting requirement is attached to the extended funds.

key_terms_explained.Special Development Fund: A dedicated development pot for the region, separate from the general operating budget.
key_terms_explained.Release: Making an appropriation available to a spending agency.
key_terms_explained.Obligation: Committing money to a contract or purchase.
key_terms_explained.Fully expended: Spent to the last peso — the condition that now ends the fund's availability, in place of a date.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Jumada Al-Akhirah 07, 1445 / 20 December 2023, approved by the Chief Minister on 29 December 2023.

benefits.headline: 4 years of development money kept alive, with no deadline to spend it.

direct_benefits.benefit: Projects funded from the 2020–2023 Special Development Funds could continue
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Communities and contractors with pending works
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Automatic — the act changes deadlines, not processes

indirect_benefits: Avoided mass lapse and re-appropriation across four budget years
limitations: No amounts stated in the act itself.
No reporting or accountability provision attached.

for_citizens: None. The act governs government spending deadlines.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management (MFBM), authorised to issue the implementing guidelines
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A road funded from the 2021 Special Development Fund is still unbuilt. Under this act the appropriation could be released and obligated to the end of 2024, and once obligated there is no date by which it must be paid.
A resident asks whether unspent development money returns to the treasury. For these funds it does not lapse on a date — it remains available until fully expended.

key_provisions: Section 1 — For the 2020 and 2021 Special Development Fund, further amends Section 3 of Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 22: all appropriations are available for release and obligation for the purpose specified until 31 December 2024, and continue to be available for disbursement until fully expended. The MFBM is authorised to issue implementing guidelines.

Section 2 — For the 2022 Special Development Fund, amends Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 23 to insert Section 48-A: all appropriations under the Special Development Fund are available for release and obligation until 31 December 2024, and continue to be available for disbursement until fully expended.

Section 3 — For the 2023 Special Development Fund, amends Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 32 to insert Section 50-B: all appropriations under the Special Development Fund are available for release and obligation until 31 December 2025, and continue to be available for disbursement until fully expended.
Section 4 — All other provisions of the laws governing these appropriations, in BAA 22, 23 and 32, remain in full force unless further amended by Parliament.
Section 6 — Takes effect immediately after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation.

who_benefits: Communities with Special Development Fund projects
impact.allocated_budget: No new appropriation. It extends the Special Development Funds appropriated by BAA 22 (2020–2021, ₱10 billion), BAA 23 (2022) and BAA 32 (2023).
impact.figures_note: The act states no amounts of its own; the sums sit in the underlying appropriations acts.

citizen_questions.q: What is the most important thing this act does?
citizen_questions.a: It removes the deadline for spending. For the 2020–2023 Special Development Funds the money continues to be available for disbursement until fully expended — there is no date on which it lapses.

citizen_questions.q: Until when can the money be committed?
citizen_questions.a: 31 December 2024 for the 2020, 2021 and 2022 funds; 31 December 2025 for the 2023 fund.
The act states no amounts. The sums are in the underlying appropriations acts — BAA 22 appropriated ₱10 billion for 2020 and 2021 alone.

citizen_questions.q: Does unspent development money go back to the treasury?
citizen_questions.a: Not on a fixed date. For these funds, availability ends only when the money is fully expended.

views.simple: Extends the Special Development Funds of 2020 to 2023, allowing commitment to end-2024 or end-2025, and removing any deadline for payment — the money stays available until fully expended.
